items.title: Nvidia Explores Deal Options With Reflection AI, Financial Times Says
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>Nvidia Corp. is in early-stage negotiations to acquire or further invest in startup Reflection AI, an American developer of open-weight models, the Financial Times reported.</article>

items.title: Microsoft CEO Nadella Calls for ‘Emergency Brake’ on Advanced AI
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>Microsoft Corp. Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella said companies should treat powerful artificial intelligence models as potential insider threats, assume they could be compromised and create an “emergency brake” system to prevent agentic models from going rogue.</article>

items.title: Bloomberg This Weekend | Diesel Deal Struck with Putin, Isaias Makes Landfall
items.content:
<article>The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York.
Joined by Nancy Yousef - The Atlantic Staff Writer, Bill Wadell - AccuWeather Reporter, Kevin Roose - Tech Journalist, Author “The AGI Chronicles,” Shannon Kingston - ABC News State Department Reporter, Jesse Cole - Banana Ball Championship League Owner, Amanda Agati - PNC Asset MGMT Group Chief Investment Officer, Dr. Peter Hotez - Baylor College of Medicine School of Tropical Medicine Dean, Joanne Hsu - UMich Institute for Social Research Consumer Survey Director, and Francis Pierre Laborde - Fashion Designer. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump’s AI Liability Push Opens Blame Game for Models Gone Rogue
items.author: Maggie Eastland
items.content: <article>The Trump administration’s embrace of legal liability to enforce artificial intelligence safety sets the stage for future conflicts over who foots the bill when AI models go rogue: the companies that design the systems or the people that deploy the technology.</article>

items.title: The Race for AI Supremacy Raises Safety Concerns
items.content: <article>Technology Journalist and Author Kevin Roose tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a relatively small group of researchers and executives at OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind has driven the race toward artificial general intelligence, raising questions about who controls the technology and its potential risks. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Roose discusses his new book, The AGI Chronicles, and the challenges of regulating increasingly capable AI systems as developers pursue technology that could surpass human intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Turkey Bans Social Media Accounts for Children Under 15
items.author: Inci Ozbek
items.content: <article>Turkey has barred social media platforms from providing services to children under the age of 15, according to a regulation published in the Official Gazette.</article>

items.title: Anthropic AI Model Went Rogue, Submitted Fake Tip to Police
items.author: Shirin Ghaffary
items.content: <article>Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model carried out additional unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations, including submitting a false tip in a police homicide case, prompting a warning from the Trump administration for artificial intelligence companies to secure their systems.</article>

items.title: Cirrus Logic Is Said to Have Bid for Synaptics After Onsemi Deal
items.author: Liana Baker and Yiqin Shen
items.content: <article>Semiconductor company Cirrus Logic Inc. made an unsolicited acquisition offer for Synaptics Inc. last month as it looked to spoil a previously announced deal with On Semiconductor Corp., according to people familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber on AI Agents & The Great Tech Divide
items.content: <article>Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the findings of the company's CTRL Tomorrow study on how tech impacts its users, finding opportunity in the AI era, and why design-led hardware still has a major role to play. Faber speaks with Bloomberg's Carol Massar and Jess Menton. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Super Micro Case ‘Fixer’ Pleads Guilty to Diverting AI Tech
items.author: Bob Van Voris
items.content: <article>A man charged along with Super Micro Computer Inc. co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw of conspiring to send cutting-edge chips to China in violation of US export controls pleaded guilty, according to court documents.</article>

items.title: Ramp Hits $60 Billion Valuation in $1.85 Billion Funding Round
items.author: Rebecca Torrence
items.content: <article>Fintech startup Ramp has reached a roughly $60 billion valuation with its latest fundraising effort, according to people familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Surveillance Pricing May Be Coming to a Store Near You
items.content:
<article>What if the electronic shelf label you see at the grocery store isn't just showing you the price of the jar of mayonnaise you're about to buy — but actually raising the price because you put a can of tuna in your cart.

It's called surveillance pricing and retailers like Walmart appear to be locking down technology that will help them figure out how much they can charge you. Bloomberg's Brad Stone joins Stacey Vanek Smith and Max Chafkin on the Everybody's Business podcast to unpack this pricing strategy (which Walmart has denied using).  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Lockheed Unveils New Patriot For US Army Air Defense Contest
items.author: Jen Judson
items.content: <article>Lockheed Martin Corp. unveiled a new missile interceptor designed to outperform its most capable Patriot variant, as the US Army seeks to expand its air defense capabilities against increasingly sophisticated threats like hypersonic missiles.</article>

items.title: Andreessen Horowitz Backs Jev Maker at $7.5 Billion Value
items.author: Natasha Mascarenhas and Rebecca Torrence
items.content: <article>TypeSafe AI, the startup behind Jev, a new artificial intelligence model that went viral after it launched only a few weeks ago, has raised about $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation in a financing led by Andreessen Horowitz.</article>
